# numax

numax is a numerical computing library for Mojo on MAX: NumPy/SciPy-named
arrays, linear algebra, FFTs, special functions, statistics, integration,
interpolation, optimization and signal processing, on CPU and GPU, with
forward-mode derivatives through the same functions.

## Install and run

- As a dependency (pixi): `numax = { git = "https://github.com/ehsanmok/numax.git" }`
  under `[dependencies]`, with `channels = ["https://conda.modular.com/max", "conda-forge"]`.
- Inside a clone of numax, every `mojo` call needs `-I .`:
  `pixi run mojo -I . file.mojo`, or `pixi run run file.mojo`.
- `docs/quickstart.md` is the shortest path to a running program.

## Where names live

- `from numax.prelude import *` -- the common surface in one import.
- `from numax import ...` -- the whole flat surface.
- One subpackage each: `numax.core` (tensors, elementwise math, logic,
  sorting), `numax.linalg`, `numax.fft`, `numax.signal`, `numax.stats`,
  `numax.special`, `numax.integrate`, `numax.interpolate`,
  `numax.optimize`, `numax.io`.
- A name is one function across both tiers: `solve(tensor)` is the device
  tier, `solve[P, 3](array)` the register tier over `Array[T, n]`; the
  argument picks the overload.

## Making tensors

| Creates | Spelling |
|---|---|
| zeros of a shape | `zeros[f32, 2, 3](ctx)`, `Static[f32, 2, 3](ctx)` |
| a shape from values | `Static[f32, 3]([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], ctx)` |
| a 1-D sequence | `linspace[5, f32](0, 1, ctx)`, `arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.25, ctx)` |
| from host data | `asarray(values, ctx)` |

`ctx` (a `DeviceContext`) is always last and optional; leaving it out is
the host. `f32` is `DType.float32`.

## Traps

1. `Tensor` is `Movable`, not `Copyable`: `var b = a` moves; `copy(a)`
   copies.
2. `dim[T, i]` is a compile-time extent in a generic signature;
   `a.dim[i]()` is the run-time one; `a.size()` is the element count.
3. Not in the prelude, because they shadow builtins: `sum`, `prod`,
   `min`, `max` (`from numax.stats import sum`), `abs`, `all`, `any`,
   `round`, `copysign` (`from numax import abs`). The distributions are
   namespaces: `from numax.stats import norm`, then `norm.cdf(...)`.
   `numax/prelude.mojo` lists each one.
4. `Tensor[...]` / `Static[...]` parameters are positional:
   `Static[f32, 2, 3]`, never `Static[dtype=f32, ...]`.
5. `Static[dtype, *dims]` has its shape in the type; `Dynamic[dtype, rank]`
   has it at run time. A routine whose output size depends on the data
   (`nonzero`, `unique`, `arange(start, stop)`) returns `Dynamic`.
6. `gpu=True` is per call; where a tensor lives is per tensor. A mismatch
   runs on the host and prints one line on stderr; `set_fallback("raise")`
   turns that into an error.
7. On Metal (Apple silicon) use `float32`: there is no `double` on the
   device.
8. A slice or block is a `TensorView` over the tensor; bind it before
   using it (`var v = a[1:3]` then `v * 2.0`) -- the inline form does not
   compile. A box narrower than the row is strided: `copy(v)` makes it
   contiguous.
9. The register tier (`Array[T, n * n]`) is for small `n`; past 64 its
   routines stop with a compile-time message naming the `Tensor`
   spelling.
10. Arguments of a `FloatLike` kernel are `T`, not `Float64`: write
    `T.constant(0.5)` for a literal.
